beginner.headline: Katherine Ryan Feels Sadness and Relief After Court Decision
beginner.brief: Comedian Katherine Ryan spoke about her feelings after Russell Brand was found guilty in court. On Thursday, the court found him guilty of two kinds of sexual crime. Ryan said she felt both sadness and relief after the court's decision. She shared how she felt on her podcast, an online show people can listen to. Ryan said she admired the people who had been hurt. Ryan said what happened would still affect their lives, whatever the court decided. Brand will learn his punishment on Monday.

intermediate.headline: Katherine Ryan Reacts to Russell Brand’s Conviction
intermediate.brief: Comedian Katherine Ryan said she felt “grief and relief” after Russell Brand was convicted of rape and sexual assault. On Thursday, the court found Brand guilty of one charge of rape and three charges of sexual assault. He was acquitted of three other charges, including two rape charges. On her podcast, Ryan said the verdict had left her emotional and that she had great respect for the survivors. She said they came forward even though Brand was famous and powerful and had fans ready to attack them. Ryan said that whatever the outcome in court, the people who had been hurt would continue to feel the effects. In an earlier TV interview, Ryan described someone in the entertainment industry as a “predator”, a person who harms others by taking advantage of them. In 2022, Ryan said she could not name the man because she believed doing so could cause legal problems. There were widespread rumours that Ryan meant Brand, but she has not confirmed that she was talking about him. Police said they were also investigating further rape allegations from two women.

advanced.headline: Katherine Ryan on Grief and Relief After Russell Brand’s Conviction
advanced.brief: Comedian Katherine Ryan described feeling both grief and relief after Russell Brand was convicted of rape and sexual assault. She said many women had been speaking privately after Thursday’s verdict and described their response as a nuanced mix of emotions. In an earlier documentary interview with Louis Theroux, Ryan had said there was a “predator” in the entertainment industry. In 2022, Ryan described naming the man as a “litigious minefield”. She said she had appeared on a television programme with him and had confronted him directly. There was speculation that Ryan was referring to her time on Roast Battle with Brand in 2018, but she has not confirmed that she meant him and did not name the programme. On her podcast, Ryan said the verdict had left her emotionally unsettled and that she was in awe of the survivors. She stressed that the survivors had come forward despite Brand’s wealth and influence and the prospect of attacks from his fans. Ryan acknowledged that some justice had been done. However much justice is done, Ryan said, those who were hurt will continue to live with the consequences. Brand was convicted on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The court acquitted him of two other rape charges and an allegation of attempted indecent assault. Ahead of Monday’s sentencing, the judge told Brand to expect a substantial custodial term, meaning a lengthy period in prison. Before the trial, Brand made an unsuccessful bid to have the case dismissed. His lawyers argued that the publicity following the Dispatches programme was so prejudicial that he could not receive a fair trial. Police said Brand was also under investigation over further rape allegations made by two women. Former BBC One controller Lorraine Heggessey questioned how Brand had avoided being held to account for so long. Heggessey suggested that one factor was Brand’s ability to draw the young viewers many broadcasters covet.
